reviews.reason: At line 220, root and contribution own the passive ShadowRoot attachment and disposal; blockId labels the mounted surface, while same-block renderInput changes go through lifecycle.update and renderEpoch only keys the React portal. Depending on renderInput would tear down live DOM on ordinary context, plan or theme updates. At line 294, the attached surface already identifies the root used to resolve the scroll owner. The blockId/surface pair owns the overlay runtime. surfaceLayoutEpoch seeds creation and is then advanced in a separate layout effect on the same runtime so its generation stays monotonic across preview/design/preview. The initial content commit notification is inside the provider and Suspense; it does not change either resource lifetime. Reassessed: Host-module resolution is now demand scoped. Committed native roots still remain while their replacement resolves, and version/owner checks keep obsolete work from publishing.

setSurface publishes the actual ShadowRoot attachment returned by mount; it is not derived state copied from props. The state enables the React portal and surface-scoped contexts only after attachment. Resource ownership follows root/contribution; ordinary input updates keep the contribution mounted, and passive disposal lets React remove its portal children before the host clears the ShadowRoot. The installed rule labels this a migration hint. The API remains supported; ref/context ABI is intentional. Native portal host deliberately separates surface mount/disposal from lifecycle.update and advanceLayoutEpoch. renderInput updates a retained contribution; layout epochs advance the existing runtime. useContext is supported in React 19. Async antd-style loading errors are resource completion failures and must be stored after the promise settles. Reassessed 2026-11-03: Every native surface now mounts AntdStyleSurfaceProvider, including transitive fetched dependencies. Retained surface/portal lifecycle and layout-epoch update boundaries remain separate; style isolation tests now cover direct, indirect and fetched module sources.

The active antd-style load can reject after render. loadError is read during render and rethrown to the enclosing FrontstageNativeTrustedBlockErrorBoundary, which reports through onRuntimeError. A ref would not schedule the render needed to surface that failure. The active guard prevents completion from publishing after cleanup. The boundary now wraps the host providers, not just the authored block, so it can catch this provider failure before initial content is acknowledged.
